```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "B's demand evidence is stronger. It has three independently sourced quotes describing real production incidents from silent or short-notice API breaking changes. A's demand rests on one sourced Reddit quote, because its second quote's URL was not retrieved and counts as missing.",
    "B's acquisition channels suit one person with little cash. A GitHub Marketplace listing and community-led growth on Reddit, HN and dev.to have near-zero cash cost and reach technical buyers where they already work. A relies on paid ads to time-poor, software-skeptical contractors. Its only figures are a generic $237 B2B SaaS blended cost per lead and an uninformative $0.01–$10+ CPC range, a cost structure the brief itself says a bootstrapped solo operator can't easily absorb.",
    "B's buyer can self-install a GitHub App and evaluate it quickly. That shortens the path to a first paying customer within 90 days compared with persuading a non-technical trades owner to trust AI-priced estimates.",
    "Both niches are crowded: 6 direct competitors for B and 7 for A. Neither brief shows a sourced differentiation wedge, so crowding does not separate them.",
    "B has real weaknesses. Several competitors are free, which caps price. False positives are documented (raw spec diffs over-report by about 8x per mendapi). Granting PR access to a third party is trust-sensitive. A has stronger willingness-to-pay evidence, with several published paid tiers at $30–$125/mo and QuotrPro's 500+ contractors. Even so, B's better demand sourcing and solo-feasible distribution outweigh this for a 90-day first-customer goal."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "A's demand evidence is effectively a single sourced quote. The second quote ('You can spend half your week driving around...') has an unretrieved URL and is listed under unsourced claims. Yet the Case for leans on both to call the pain 'quantified by contractors themselves.' The claim that EstimationPro and Outdoor Estimates are run by single contractor-founders is also unsupported by any source in the brief.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. A has clearly better willingness-to-pay evidence: higher published price points and a competitor traction number. B faces real price pressure from free competitors, and the brief openly asks whether SMBs will pay. B's community-channel CAC figure comes from a page containing a prompt-injection attempt, so it was treated as directional only and given no weight. The decision rests mainly on sourced demand quotes and solo-feasible acquisition, which favor B."
}
```
